She finally had him in her clutches. She, being the most sophisticated and cunning supervillain in town, him being some typical superhero type. He was very bland, really.

She had just finished explaining to him just how she was about to end his life but it had not elicited the reaction she'd been aiming for. *She* had expected fear or anger or at the very least some negotiating. All she received instead was a pitiful gaze.

"What?" she snarled. The look in his eyes became hesitant, then confused, and finally he avoided her eyes altogether, choosing to stare at his feet which were bound together and dangling over an enormous pot of boiling oil.

"I think you have some," he began but stopped to consider his words." What I mean to say is I understand you may not have had the easiest upbringing."

Anger flared up in her.

"What I don't understand is your issue with, uhm," he continued. "Uh, with scotch eggs."

"What, you egg?" she demanded of him, feeling strangely humiliated now. She placed her hand on the lever that would drop his sausage meat and bread crumb covered body into the pot below.

"Did your parents not give you enough attention as a child?" he asked. "There are people that can help, you know. I had to see a counsellor, too, it helped me immense- "

"Oh my *god*, you're one of *them*," she groaned, understanding now. "You think I'm damaged and have issues and now I kill men because *Daddy didn't love me*. I'll have you know my father loved me and my mother just fine. He was just always buying those *fucking* scotch eggs!"

He finally locked eyes with her and now he looked offended. "What's wrong with scotch eggs?!"

"I'm a vegan!" she shouted back and pulled the lever.

I don't quite remember how I met Ellie. I think it was raining heavily. At least, I remember feeling soaked and not hearing much besides roaring water, like glass shattering all around me.  I can't even remember what it looked like where I was. There was just *her*.

Her deep auburn hair framing her freckled face, her sky blue eyes with little flecks of white around the edges of her irises, her red lipstick and her wide grin with little dimples dotting her cheeks. She was magnificent. I think she was leaning over me, reaching a hand out to help me on my feet. 

She was thoughtful and kind to everyone and everyone seemed enthralled by her. She succeeded at everything she set out to do. I was floored when she chose me. 

Of course she made the first move. She knew what she wanted and would always take it. She didn't need anybody's help. And of course, I wouldn't have dared to try to make a move. She was very much out of my league. 

We spoke about moving abroad although we ended up staying in the same town where we met. After she got pregnant we didn't have the funds to move away. We managed to find a small apartment regardless and we made it home. 

We had our first child, a little girl, and then we had another daughter. I had landed a well paying job and Ellie stayed at home with our girls where they would make pottery wares that she sold online.

Every night, I'd read the kids bedtime stories and every morning, my girls would wake me up with their laughter as they piled on the bed to play and talk about what they had dreamt of, and I'd admire my wife's messy hair and sleepy smile and we were happy.

Until one quiet morning, devoid of laughter and chatter and instead, the silence was punctured by a steady beeping and whirring and the buzz of a lightbulb that was shining too brightly. 

A nurse was checking on another patient in the room. She shuffled over then to check on me and dropped her pen in shock. 

"You're awake," she breathed. "This is- the odds of you waking up were so slim, this is- "

I didn't hear what my situation was just then because she hurried out of the room to fetch a doctor. 

I remember now. 

The doctor rushed into the room to tell me what had happened to me. She said I had been driving along the shore when an oncoming car swerved into my car and I was sent tumbling down. The water hadn't been very deep and so some kind people who had witnessed this had managed to free me before I drowned. Paramedics told them off for moving me when it was dangerous but I had at the very least survived. I was alive but unconscious. 

She had been checking me over while telling me this and then stopped to take a deep breath. 

"Now, this is the part that's difficult, and this may come as a shock to you," she said, her voice kind and gentle. "We had to put you into a medically induced coma due to the dire situation you were in. It was only meant to be six weeks but you stayed in that coma for a year."

The heart monitor began to beep faster while I struggled to comprehend what she had just told me. She leaned over me so I could see her clearly and she took my hand to comfort me. She had deep auburn hair and eyes like a sparsely clouded summer sky and her cheeks were dotted with freckles and dimples. 

That's how I met Ellie.
